Artabimus igitur Judaeos, qui de otio sabbati gloriantur, quod jam tunc in principio sabbatum dissolutum sit, dum Deus operatur in sabbato, complens opera sua in eo, et benedicens ipsi diei, quia in illo universa compleverit.” The same. Hieron.: “For _the sixth day_ the Hebrew has _the seventh day_. ius, Symmachum in mente habuisse nomen φυλή, _tribus, gens;_ ut _Pamphylia_ sit regio a variis gentibus habitata, juxta Judaeorum opinionem a Jarchio memoratam: “גּוֹיִם, locus ita dictus, quod eo convenissent plurimae nationes, quae regem constituerunt super se, nomine Tidal.” Procop. Cf. on v. 9. Not unreasonably Drusius conjectures that Symmachus had in mind the noun φυλή, _tribe, nation;_ so that _Pamphylia_ would be a region inhabited by various nations, according to the opinion of the Jews mentioned by Jarchi: “גּוֹיִם, a place so called because very many nations had gathered there, who set up a king over themselves, by name Tidal.”

aqua inventa est, Isaac ad nomen civitatis, quae ita vocabatur, alludens, declinavit paululum literam, et pro stridulo Hebraeorum SIN, a quo SABEC incipitur, Graecum SIGMA, id est, Hebraeum SAMECH posuit.” Hieron.: “I do not know how it is found in the LXX translators … _And they said to him: We have not found water; and he called its name Oath._ For what etymology is it, to be called _oath_ because they had not found water? On the contrary, in the Hebrew, with which interpretation Aq. also and Sym. agree, the meaning is that they found water, and that therefore the well itself was called _Fulness_, and the city was called Bersabee, that is, _well of fulness._

Ο΄. παγιδεύεις. Ἀ. ἐγκρούεις.^18 _Insidiaris._ Cod. 243. Respexit interpres Chaldaeum נְקַשׁ, _percussit, pulsavit_ (cf. Dan. v. 6 in Chald. et Theod.), necnon Syriacum ܢܩܫ, quod pro Graeco ἐνέκρουσεν posuit Paulus Telensis Jud. iv. 21. Cf. Hex. ad Psal. cviii. 11. Cod. 243. The translator had in view the Chaldee נְקַשׁ, “_he struck, knocked_” (cf. Dan. v. 6 in the Chald. and Theod.), and also the Syriac ܢܩܫ, which Paul of Tella put for the Greek ἐνέκρουσεν in Jud. iv. 21. Cf. Hex. on Psal. cviii. 11.

key: ※ Θ. καὶ τὸν οἶκον τοῦ βασιλέως, καὶ τὸν οἶκον τοῦ λαοῦ ἐνέπρησαν οἱ Χαλδαῖοι ἐν πυρὶ, καὶ τὸ τεῖχος Ἱερουσαλὴμ καθεῖλον.^18

Jes., ceteri, nisi quod Codd. 22, 36, alii, καὶ τοὺς οἴκους τοῦ λαοῦ, exhibent. In fine Montef. edidit: καὶ τὸ τεῖχος τῆς Ἱερ. καθεῖλον, invitis ceteris. key: Ο΄. εἰς οἶκον κυρίου. Σ. εἰσέτι ὄντα καὶ ἐλπιζόμενον.^16
candidates.excerpt: , vel etiam ipsius interpretis explicatio, qua innuitur, domum Dei, etsi combustam et dirutam, opinione ac spe fidelium Judaeorum adhuc exsistere. Cod. 86. It seems to be a scholion, or even an explanation of the translator himself, by which it is intimated that the house of God, although burnt and destroyed, still existed in the opinion and hope of the faithful Jews.

key: Ο΄. ἐν μέσῳ τοῦ λαοῦ σου. Ἑβρ. ἠχαλάχ.^24 Ἀ. Σ. Θ. Ε΄. Ϛ΄. ἐν μέσῳ τοῦ ναοῦ σου.^25
candidates.excerpt: us vertimus, _templi tui_, in Graeco vos legisse dicitis, _populi tui_, quod superfluum est. In Hebraico scriptum est ECHALACH, id est, τοῦ ναοῦ σου, et non AMMACH, quod _populum tuum_ significat.” Etiam in Syro-hex. est τοῦ λαοῦ σου. Chrysost. Jerome in his Epistle to Sun. and Fret. 28: “Where we have translated from the Hebrew and from the LXX translators _of thy temple_, you say you read in the Greek _of thy people_, which is superfluous. In the Hebrew is written ECHALACH, that is, τοῦ ναοῦ σου, and not AMMACH, which means _thy people_.” In Syro-hex. too there is τοῦ λαοῦ σου. Nobil., Vat. Nobil., Vat.

key: Ο΄. καὶ ἠγάπησαν αὐτὸν ἐν τῷ στόματι αὐτῶν. Σ. καὶ ὡς παραλογιζόμενοι αὐτὸν ὑπελάμβανον (s. ᾤοντο) ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτῶν.^36
candidates.excerpt: a notione Dei ἀνθρωποπαθοῦς, v. c., qui fraude circumveniri posset, quam longissime abhorrere. Vid. D. Abr. Geiger in _Jüdische Zeitschrift_ etc. p. 45. Syro-hex. ܣ. ܘܐܝܟ ܡܛܥܝܢ ܠܗ ܡܣܬܒܪܝܢ ܗܘܘ ܒܠܒܗܘܢ܀. A freer version than is customary even with Symmachus, unless it be assumed that this translator shrank as far as possible from the notion of an ἀνθρωποπαθοῦς God, e.g. one who could be circumvented by fraud. key: Ο΄. εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα δι᾽ ἀντάμειψιν. Σ. εἰς μισθαποδοσίαν αἰώνιον.^94
candidates.excerpt: em mercedis aeternam_, quasi scriptum esset ܠܦܘܪܥܢܘܬ ܐܓܪܐ, quod verum puto. Pro μισθαποδοσία Hebr. ii. 2 etc. interpres Philox. posuit ܦܘܪܥܢ ܐܓܪܐ. Montef. quidem ex uno cod. affert: Σ. δι᾽ ἀνταπόδοσιν, quod sine titulo legitur in marg. Cod. 268, et merum scholium esse videtur. The same: ܣ. ܠܦܘܪܥܢܘܬܐ ܐܓܪܐ ܕܠܥܠܡ܀. Bugati renders: _for an eternal recompense of reward_, as if ܠܦܘܪܥܢܘܬ ܐܓܪܐ were written, which I think is correct. For μισθαποδοσία Hebr. ii. 2 etc. the Philox. translator put ܦܘܪܥܢ ܐܓܪܐ. Montef. indeed cites from one manuscript: Σ. δι᾽ ἀνταπόδοσιν, which is read without title in the margin of Cod. 268, and seems to be a mere scholion.

key: Ο΄. αἰνεῖτε αὐτὸν ἐν στερεώματι δυνάμεως αὐτοῦ. Ἀ. . . ἐν στερεώματι κράτους αὐτοῦ.^2 Σ. ὑμνεῖτε αὐτὸν ἐν τῷ στερεώματι τῷ ἀκαθαιρέτῳ αὐτοῦ.^3
candidates.excerpt: ς δὲ ἀντὶ τοῦ, ἐν στερεώματι, τῷ ἀκαθαιρέτῳ εἶπε. Tandem Syro-hex.: Σ. τῷ ἀκαθαιρέτῳ (ܠܐ ܡܬܣܬܪܢܐ[?]) αὐτοῦ; cum scholio philologico: ܠܐ ܡܬܗܦܟܢܐ[?]܀, _quod everti non potest._ Colb., written στιχηρῶς. Theodoret. gives: Σ. αἰνεῖτε αὐτὸν ἐν στερεώματι κ.τ.ἑ. Two Regii, from Chrysostom's exposition, have: Σ. οἱ ὄντες ἐν τῷ στ. τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἄγγελοι, ὑμνεῖτε αὐτὸν κ.τ.ἑ. Less probably Chrysost.: Ἕτερος δὲ ἀντὶ τοῦ, ἐν στερεώματι, τῷ ἀκαθαιρέτῳ εἶπε. Finally Syro-hex.: Σ. τῷ ἀκαθαιρέτῳ (ܠܐ ܡܬܣܬܪܢܐ[?]) αὐτοῦ; with a philological scholium: ܠܐ ܡܬܗܦܟܢܐ[?]܀, _which cannot be overthrown._
